intent:
In this repository and in loop-harness, knowledge stays current because of things kmctl does not ship: 23 rule files loaded by path, a `CLAUDE.md` that routes to `.okf/`, a seeded bundle agents copy, and a reviewer whose consistency lens reads those rules. A fresh `kmctl init` writes four files and nothing else, so an agent gets a briefing and empty templates. `kmctl init` changes to seed the habit, never overwriting a file the repository already has:

- Rules as files: it writes the knowledge rules `okf-bundle`, `docs-layout`, `diagrams-stay-current` and `manifesto-invariants` to `.claude/rules/`, in full with their WHY paragraphs and `paths:` front matter, from package data. The packaged copies are written for any repository: no mention of loopctl, tickets or this repository's own files. They are separate package data from the briefing's rules: the briefing keeps exactly its two one-line rules from `src/kmctl/rules/`, unchanged, because it is at 526 of its 600 words and the two new rules would take it past the budget (I3; round 1 plan review). The CLAUDE.md block's duties carry the gist of the two new rules for every harness that reads it. An existing rule file of the same name is kept and reported.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`: it adds a block between `<!-- kmctl:start -->` and `<!-- kmctl:end -->` holding the routing table (what goes in `docs/`, the manifesto, `decisions/`, `architecture/` and the rest) and three duties: record each choice as a decision when it is made, keep `architecture/` matching the code, and run `kmctl check` before finishing. The block goes into each of `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` that exists, once per real file, so a `CLAUDE.md` that is a symlink to `AGENTS.md` gets one block; with neither file, it writes `CLAUDE.md` with the block. In a file that has the block already, it replaces only the block; otherwise it appends it. No other text in either file changes.
- First decision: when no record in the decisions folder already has the title "Keep project knowledge in an OKF bundle", it records it as the next decision (0001 in a fresh bundle), "Keep project knowledge in an OKF bundle", in the target repository's decisions folder through `kmctl new decision`'s writer, with real Context, Decision (the rejected alternatives: a wiki, README-only notes, nothing), and Consequences, plus its index entry and log line.
- A new decision record in this repository says init now writes `.claude/rules/` and a `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` block, which reverses the alternative ADR 0002 rejected (native rule files per harness) for Claude Code only (ADR 0003), and keeps the briefing as the cross-harness path; ADR 0002 gets an appended dated Correction pointing to it. Init's "never edits a kept file" promise, in `ScaffoldResult`'s docstring and the help text, changes to name the one exception: the kmctl block in those two files, plus the index entry and log line for the first decision.
- Next steps: its output ends with what the agent does next, in order: fill the manifesto's purpose and invariants (values are the operator's), add an architecture page once there is code, and record each choice with `kmctl new decision`.

Measured on the operator's failing session: the agent made 6 design choices and recorded 1, wrote 0 architecture pages, and left the manifesto's values empty; a fresh `kmctl init` today writes 0 rule files, 0 lines of `CLAUDE.md` and 0 decisions.

Done when tests show init writes the four rule files with their front matter and keeps an existing one; writes, appends to, or replaces only its block in `CLAUDE.md` and in `AGENTS.md` when it exists, once through a symlink; the briefing's text is unchanged; writes the first decision with its sections, index entry and log line, and writes no second copy when a record with its title exists (on a second run, or in a bundle that already has decisions numbered past 0001), and `kmctl check` and the strict okf validator pass right after init; prints the next steps; and running init twice changes nothing the second time. A spike reruns spike 1's task with the built `kmctl init` and the real SessionStart briefing, and counts decisions recorded and architecture pages written against spike 1's arms.

# init-seeds-the-habit

Relayed from: operator, 2026-10-15, after an agent in a kmctl repository wrote code and left the bundle nearly empty: rules "should be included either as briefing or by CLI writing them using init"; "CLAUDE.md --> either append when doing init or write if it doesn't exist"; "Instruct the agent when initing to write manifesto, record architectural choices, and CLI init should write first decision to capture knowledge in .okf / use OKF".

## Could invalidate this plan

- Settled for this setup by spike:init-seeds-the-habit/1: on one FastAPI task with three runs per arm, seeding raised architecture pages from 0 of 3 runs to 3 of 3 and decisions from a mean of 3.0 to 4.3, with `kmctl check` passing in all six. The unseeded arm did not reproduce the operator's 1-of-6 failure, likely because the briefing went in the prompt text there, so the decision gain is the smaller result.
